conversation.content:
```markdown
I’m going to ask you 10 short questions that help us check in on how you’re feeling and coping in the past seven days.  // пример, как выглядит передаётся внешне; просто продолжайте
```
Okay, I’m ready.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I might smile if something is really cute with the baby, but most of the time I just feel too worn-out to find anything funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much... I used to get excited about little things, like a quiet cup of coffee or a walk, but lately even those feel kind of pointless. I still try to go through the motions, but the enjoyment just isn’t really there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I keep thinking I should be doing everything better. When he won’t settle or I can’t get the feeding right, it feels like it’s my fault for not knowing what he needs. I tell myself I’m failing him, even if my partner says I’m doing fine.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes. My heart races even when the baby is sleeping peacefully. I’ll lie there imagining the cot could tip or the milk might scald him, and I can’t stop checking the monitor even though I know he’s safe.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I do get those waves of panic—like I’m not breathing right or the room is closing in. It hits out of nowhere, even when everything seems fine, and then I feel silly for getting so worked up.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah… I’ll be feeding the baby and see the laundry pile or dirty bottles and feel like I’m drowning. I keep telling myself to just tackle one thing at a time, but it still feels as though I’m always behind and can’t catch my breath.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
Exactly. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs.” I’ll finally drift off, then every squeak from the crib jolts me awake and I can’t settle again for ages.
I have felt sad or miserable
Pretty much every day. I’ll be holding the baby and tears just well up for no clear reason. It’s like there’s a gray cloud that won’t lift, even when I know I should feel grateful.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

That’s been me most evenings—little things set me off, like running out of muslin cloths or seeing other mums laughing on social media. The tears come and I can’t stop them; feels like the easiest release, even though I hate feeling so weepy over “small stuff.”
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… never. Even on my worst nights, when I feel useless and overwhelmed, I know I’d never do anything like that. My baby needs me, and I want to be here for him.

You have shared how every day lately feels heavy: constant <sym>tearfulness</sym> and a <sym>low mood</sym> that clouds even sweet moments with your baby, <sym>panic attacks</sym> that arrive without warning, and nights spent lying awake running through frightening "what-ifs". You describe feeling overwhelmed by ordinary tasks, blaming yourself whenever anything feels hard, and finding little enjoyment in things you used to like. Even though you love your baby deeply and would never consider self-harm, the emotional exhaustion is real and you deserve support.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 22, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports diminished enjoyment—smiles rarely at cute moments, but generally too worn-out to laugh, matching option 2.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes diminished enjoyment matching "Hardly at all"</sym>, <sym>Patient acknowledges frequent self-blame linked to infant-care struggles, mapping to 'some of the time</sym>, <sym>The mother describes frequent, intrusive mental images of the infant in danger (cot tipping, milk scalding) and compulsive monitor-checking despite knowing the baby is safe.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent, sudden panic episodes with physical symptoms and no clear trigger, matching "Yes, quite a lot"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent overwhelm ('most days'), feeling 'drowning' and 'always behind,' matching 'sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent sleep disruption due to racing thoughts and hyper-alertness, matching 'Yes, sometimes</sym>, <sym>Patient describes daily sadness and unexplained crying, matching "most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports crying "most evenings," triggered by minor stressors and feeling unable to stop, matching "Yes, most of the time"</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Your EPDS total of 22 places you well above the threshold (≥14) indicating probable <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med> plus co-occurring <med>anxiety</med>. You endorse core symptoms matching <med>DSM-5</med> criteria: depressed mood most of the day, markedly diminished interest or pleasure, feelings of worthlessness/guilt, and insomnia nearly every day for the past two weeks. <sym>Spontaneous panic</sym> and compulsive checking suggest comorbid <med>anxiety disorder</med>. There is no current suicidal ideation, a positive protective factor. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with your <med>GP</med>/obstetric provider or <med>perinatal mental health team</med> within the next few days
2. Ask about evidence-based treatments for <med>postpartum depression</med> such as <med>CBT</med> or sertraline compatible with breastfeeding
3. Share results with your partner or trusted family so they can help with night care and household tasks while you recover
4. Begin gentle daily routine: daylight walk, nutritious snacks every 3h, and 20-min rest when baby sleeps to support circadian rhythm
5. Use a simple mood log or app to track sleep hours, panic frequency, and moments of enjoyment for discussion at your follow-up visit
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Patient-reported symptoms (≥2 wks unless noted):

Affective  
• Persistent low mood, tearfulness daily  
• Marked anhedonia—loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities

Cognitive  
• Pervasive self-blame/guilt regarding infant care (“I’m failing him”)  
• “What-if” rumination, especially about infant safety

Anxiety spectrum  
• Unprovoked anxious arousal (heart racing, room “closing in”)  
• Panic-like episodes occurring “out of nowhere”  
• Excessive checking of baby monitor despite acknowledged safety

Functional/neuro-vegetative  
• Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia secondary to racing thoughts  
• Feeling “drowning” or “can’t catch breath” when viewing routine tasks

Safety  
• Denies any self-harm ideation; protective factor = desire to care for infant

Pattern summary  
Responses cluster strongly with perinatal depression (sad mood, anhedonia, guilt, tearfulness, sleep disruption) with co-occurring anxiety symptoms (panic, intrusive worries). No suicidal ideation elicited.

Screening significance  
Elevated probability for Major Depressive Disorder with peripartum onset and co-morbid anxiety; warrants follow-up with structured diagnostic interview and consideration of perinatal mental-health referral for comprehensive assessment and intervention planning.
